title: Use an App token, not GITHUB_TOKEN, when the event must trigger another workflow or reach another repo
answers: Why does my workflow not trigger after a GITHUB_TOKEN comment or label change?
When do I need actions/create-github-app-token instead of secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN?
Can GITHUB_TOKEN access another repository from a GitHub Actions job?
Which token should a workflow use to post a comment that starts another workflow?
body:
Invariant: default to `${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}` for same-repo operations within the job's `permissions:`. Events created with GITHUB_TOKEN generally do not start new workflow runs, so when a comment, label, or push must trigger another workflow, use a token from `actions/create-github-app-token`.
GITHUB_TOKEN is also scoped to the current repository, so cross-repository access needs an App token too.
Enforced by: .claude/rules/github-actions.md (section "Prefer `GITHUB_TOKEN` When Its Scope and Trigger Behavior Are Sufficient"); the App-token patterns in .github/workflows/build-docs.yml (cross-repo access) and .github/workflows/ui-review.yml (step-level privilege isolation).
What breaks: swapping an App token for GITHUB_TOKEN silently suppresses downstream workflow runs, or the cross-repo/privileged step fails on permissions.
Scope: the rule's "unless triggering" framing is not the only reason for an App token; do not replace App tokens that serve cross-repo access or step isolation.
applies: GitHub Actions workflow authoring under .github/workflows/ and the agent rules in .claude/rules/.
says: Downstream automated pipelines fail to run after a bot posts a comment.
Automated label changes on a pull request did not start our follow-up workflows.
Documentation builds failed with permission errors when attempting to access an external repository.
Why did our automated release commit not trigger the downstream deployment pipeline?
Allow automated pull request updates to trigger subsequent continuous integration jobs.
search: GitHub Actions workflows must use tokens from actions/create-github-app-token instead of secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN when events must trigger downstream workflows, access external repositories, or isolate step privileges. Same-repo operations should default to secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN within job permissions, as events created with it generally do not trigger new runs. Applies to workflow authoring in .github/workflows/ and guidance in .claude/rules/github-actions.md, referencing patterns in .github/workflows/build-docs.yml and .github/workflows/ui-review.yml. App tokens must not be replaced with GITHUB_TOKEN if they are serving cross-repository access or step-level privilege isolation.
